validated_results.title: Urinary bladder cancer risk factors: a Lebanese case- control study.
validated_results.journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
validated_results.reason: Human hospital-based case-control study of bladder cancer risk factors that assessed tea consumption as one of the dietary exposures in relation to incident bladder cancer diagnoses.

extraction.comparison_type: Tea consumption in cases vs controls (no quantitative contrast reported)
extraction.population: Patients from two major hospitals in Beirut

sample_size.excerpt: A case-control study (54 cases and 105 hospital-based controls) was conducted in two major hospitals in Beirut. Cases were randomly selected from patients diagnosed in the period of 2002-2008.

cases.excerpt: A case-control study (54 cases and 105 hospital-based controls) was conducted in two major hospitals in Beirut. Cases were randomly selected from patients diagnosed in the period of 2002-2008.

design.excerpt: A case-control study (54 cases and 105 hospital-based controls) was conducted in two major hospitals in Beirut.

ethnicity.excerpt: This is the first case-control study investigating bladder cancer risk factors in the Lebanese context.
